Definition: from G2799; lamentation:--wailing, weeping, X wept.
KeyPassages: Matthew 2:18; Matthew 8:12; Matthew 13:42; Matthew 13:50; Luke 13:28; Acts 20:37
BiblicalUsage: Klauthmos is wailing, weeping aloud. Matthew 2:18 hears lamentation and weeping and great mourning, Rachel weeping for her children, Matthew 8:12 and Matthew 13:42 and Matthew 13:50 and Luke 13:28 all warn of outer darkness where there shall be weeping and gnashing of teeth, and Acts 20:37 shows the other side: the elders of Ephesus wept sore, and fell on Paul's neck, and kissed him.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe klauthmos holds two wailings that must never be confused: the wailing of those cast out, and the weeping of those who love Paul and will not see his face again. I hold that the first is judgment and the second is love, and the Bible lets both sound at full volume.
